🚀 Feature

I think it will be more convenient if PyTorch can combine the operation of with torch.no_grad() into the net.eval().
Motivation

When I was using PyTorch, I found it strange as I needed using the operations of with torch.no_grad() and the net.eval(), because I had thought the function net.eval() would complete the operation of closing the gradient passing in the parameters in my model, as its name eval().
And I think, when using the model to infer the results, we tend to close the gradient updating.
So I am wondering whether there are some other reasons for you to separate the with torch.no_grad() from net.eval().
Pitch

That is, I just need to use net.eval() to change my model code into the state of validation, without the gradient updating, and do not need to use the code with torch.no_grad() extra.
Alternatives

Additional context

I am also wondering that there may be some other reasons for you to separate the with torch.no_grad() from net.eval(), and I hope you can tell me the scenarios where the separating would not be suitable.

For ProcessGroupAgent, there is a message counter matching to ensure all in-flight messages are finished before shutting down Agent. For other RpcAgent, there is no similar thing. So we want to eliminate RpcAgent::join(), by adding a common utility to do RPC-based barrier + shutdown in #30710.
Even with #30710, trying remove agent.join() uncovers that RRefs could be leaking, because the user workers might not have sent out the delete fork messages before they shut down RPC locally.
Now, sending out RRef fork delete messages solely depends on Python GC timing. We need to add an API in the RRefContext, to proactively send out delete fork message before shutting down the RPC layer on local. Only with this feature, there is no sporadic RRef leak for other RPC agents.
Now other RPC agents hide this RRef leak by sleeping for 2 seconds on shutting down, so that Python GC can trigger the messages.
It was also surfaced in #30022. When closing this issue, make sure the case mentioned in that issue is also covered.

Tests from #31147 have uncovered a couple of silent autograd errors where wrong gradients are computed.
The process to fix these:

 Add a way to forbid rebasing the history of a given Tensor.
 Codegen functions that return at least a view and multiple output should make sure that their history cannot be rebased (unbind, split etc) or that we are in a case where we always compute correct gradients.
 Custom autograd.Function that returns a view of a Tensor that was created inside the forward will lead to wrong gradients. Differentiable views created when grad mode is disabled should not allow their history to be rebased: #26546
 Custom autograd.Function ignore the .mark_dirty() if the input that is marked is not returned as is.
 Custom autograd.Function that perform views will have their .backward() ignored if an inplace operation is performed on their output.
 Custom autograd.Function are allowed to return views and multiple outputs: #13452

my_class_rref = rpc.remote("worker1", torch.add, args=(torch.ones(1),torch.ones(1))

buted/rpc/py_rref.cpp:74)

Note that worker0 should be worker1 in the error message.

nodes.bodyText:
I'm noticing that we're getting vtables generated for some classes that subclass intrusive_ptr_target. This is a bit surprising, because in the case I was looking at (VersionCounter), the vtable is totally unnecessary: the class is final and doesn't define any virtual methods itself.
"OK Edward, maybe it's technically unnecessary, but why does it matter?" Well, I noticed this because I was debugging UBSAN errors in #28536 and I noticed UBSAN was whinging about how I was doing an invalid downcast of torch::autograd::AutogradMeta to torch::autograd::AutogradMeta. The reason this happened was because the typeinfo for AutogradMeta was a weak symbol, and present in both libtorch_cpu.so and my_extension_lib.so; with RTLD_LOCAL that means that I end up with this symbol linked twice, and now the typeinfos aren't pointer equal and UBSAN gets pissy at me. And the reason the typeinfo is a weak symbol is because there's a virtual method on this class... and that's intrusive_ptr_target's fault.
In fact, in our cpp extension test, I count four typeinfos that have weak symbols because of intrusive ptr target:
0000000000030770 V typeinfo for at::Tensor (at::Tensor, at::Tensor)
0000000000030780 V typeinfo for bool (c10::optional<at::Tensor>)
0000000000030800 V typeinfo for c10::VariableVersion::VersionCounter
00000000000307d8 V typeinfo for c10::bad_optional_access
00000000000307f0 V typeinfo for c10::intrusive_ptr_target
00000000000307c0 V typeinfo for c10::Error
0000000000030818 V typeinfo for c10::detail::ListImpl<long>
0000000000030830 V typeinfo for torch::autograd::AutogradMeta
00000000000308e8 V typeinfo for at::Tensor (*)(at::Tensor, at::Tensor)
0000000000030908 V typeinfo for bool (*)(c10::optional<at::Tensor>)
0000000000030760 V typeinfo for std::_Mutex_base<(__gnu_cxx::_Lock_policy)2>
00000000000307a8 V typeinfo for std::_Sp_counted_base<(__gnu_cxx::_Lock_policy)2>
00000000000308d0 V typeinfo for std::_Sp_counted_deleter<c10::OperatorKernel*, std::default_delete<c10::OperatorKernel>, std::allocator<void>, (__gnu_cxx::_Lock_policy)2>

To make sure UBSAN doesn't choke to death, I have to ensure that I write subclasses of intrusive_ptr_target in such a way that the "key method" heuristic (https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Vague-Linkage.html) specifies that I don't have to splat a typeinfo in every use site of the class. I cannot imagine the average user of intrusive_ptr_target will get this right. Better to just make intrusive_ptr_target non-virtual, as it logically should be.
(Technically, we still have this pointer problem if we ever use RTTI on our types in question. But here the solution is simpler: DON'T use RTTI.)
cc @smessmer

Some tests need to validate equality with low precision. The most common use-case is when testing operations on low-precision dtypes like torch.half or torch.bfloat16. There are a number of ways we handle this in testing code:
